title: Cross-model KV source × target factorization with whole ordered-pair holdout
hypothesis: A canonical rank-32 cache-map basis plus a low-rank CP functional coordinate over source-model identity × target-model identity × normalized target layer/head/KV role can predict unseen ordered cache-transfer pairs without fitting a pair-specific map. On two fresh ordered pairs, predictions will remain within +0.50 nat of independent weighted ridge and within +1.00 nat of native target prefill while using at least 50% fewer serialized bridge bytes than independent maps.
prior_art_boundary: PA236/PA237 establish pair-dependent per-pair closed-form bridge controls. MA-876 tests a shared PCA basis with heldout-pair code fit; MA-880 tests source×target model factors that predict a whole unseen direction without heldout-pair calibration. This is not a CacheBridge reproduction.
physical_object: Per-target-layer/head/KV affine cache maps, represented by a shared rank-32 PCA basis and source×target×role low-rank coefficients.
logical_multiplicity: Ordered model-pair cache translators generated from one source factor table, one target factor table and normalized role factors.
mirror_coordinate: Rank-Q CP product of source-model, target-model and normalized target-role factors, decoded through shared rank-32 map atoms.

pair_partition.invariant: All four model IDs appear as source and target in training pairs. No development or fresh ordered pair is used to fit the source×target factors.

controls: Independent per-pair attention-weighted affine ridge maps fit on that pair calibration prompts
Rank-32 shared PCA basis fit only on training pairs, with heldout pair-specific calibration-map coefficients (diagnostic control)

fixed_design.position: inverse source RoPE on keys before fit; target RoPE after key mapping; values unrotated
fixed_design.cp_objective: mean squared error of standardized training-pair rank-32 map codes plus 1e-5 factor L2 penalty; means and scales are paid serialized state

development.selection: lowest mean factor-predicted target next-token NLL over the two whole development pairs; tie to smaller CP rank

fresh.prompt_eligibility: 16–128 tokens and exact source/target tokenizer character-offset equality
fresh.selection: Three fixed disjoint chunks from the first 36 aligned rows per pair, deterministic pair-specific permutation

primary_metrics: NLL delta versus native target prefill
NLL delta versus full independent pair ridge
NLL delta versus heldout-pair PCA code control
success_gate: For both fresh heldout pairs in all three seeds, factor NLL is no more than +0.50 nat from independent full-map NLL and no more than +1.00 nat from native target NLL; aggregate factor payload for both logical pairs is at least 50% smaller than the aggregate independent full-map payload.
failure_gate: Any quality or storage gate miss. Also report separately if full independent maps themselves are >+1.00 nat from native; this means the transfer application is not useful at this scope.
mirror_specific_boundary: The CP source×target×role decoder is an ordinary tensor-factorization control. Any match is a native low-rank factorization alias and cannot be claimed as Mirror-specific.

storage.common_model_weights: reported separately; excluded from marginal translator payload

compute.hardware: CPU-only expected; no GPU serving claim.

scope: Four cached pretrained models; eight directed pairs partitioned into four train, two development and two fresh pairs.
Wikitext-2, one-token next-token probes, fixed relative depth/head assignment and 64-dimensional head maps.
No multi-token generation trajectory, long-context serving, GPU latency or universal pair generalization claim.

protocol_amendments.timing: after initial development, before the amended development rerun and before any fresh split access
protocol_amendments.change: Initial raw-code development showed poorly conditioned coefficients (train code MSE about 9.8e5) and weak CP optimization. Standardize each PCA coefficient using mean/std computed only from training-pair map codes; serialize and charge these vectors; retain the same ranks, 600 updates, optimizer, pairs, prompt counts and selection rule.

protocol_amendments.timing: after first fresh run, before an identical diagnostic replay
protocol_amendments.change: Add per-world wall time, heldout full-map calibration time and fixed role-grid serializer metadata bytes. The replay uses the same frozen Q=1, model pairs, prompt IDs, calibration maps, seeds and 600 updates; it adds compute/accounting fields only and preserves the initial output.

protocol_amendments.timing: after fresh implementation-deviation results were inspected; before corrected development and corrected fresh replay
protocol_amendments.change: Code review found the initial MA-880 implementation omitted the protocol-declared inverse-source/inverse-target RoPE operations during ridge fitting and target RoPE application during decoding. Preserve the initial outputs and serialized payloads as `*_unrotated_deviation` evidence, do not use them to select settings, implement the already frozen position rule, rerun development on train only to reselect CP rank, then run the corrected fresh worlds with unchanged pair partition, prompt counts and gates. GPT-2 uses absolute positions and receives no RoPE transform.

post_fresh_deviation_disposition: Initial raw-position implementation output is preserved but excluded from the official corrected result. Corrected result uses the already declared RoPE protocol after train-only dev reselection; same fresh row IDs were replayed, so this is an amended diagnostic and not an independent audit.
